question:
(a) Compare refraction at a plane surface with refraction at a spherical surface.
(b) Light from air is incident on a spherical glass surface of refractive index $1.5$ and radius of curvature $20\,\text{cm}$. If the object is at $100\,\text{cm}$ from the surface, calculate the image position.

options.A:
(a) At a plane surface and a spherical surface, refraction gives identical image relations and curvature has no effect.
(b) Taking $u=+100\,\text{cm}$ and $R=-20\,\text{cm}$ gives $v=-100\,\text{cm}$.
options.B:
(a) A plane surface has a centre of curvature and focuses rays like a spherical surface.
(b) $\dfrac{1.5}{v}-\dfrac{1}{-100}=\dfrac{1.5-1}{20}$ gives $v=150\,\text{cm}$.
options.C:
(a) At a plane surface, light refracts according to Snell's law, but there is no centre of curvature. At a spherical surface, the normal changes from point to point through the centre of curvature, so $u,v,R,n_1,n_2$ determine image position.
(b) With $n_1=1$, $n_2=1.5$, $u=-100\,\text{cm}$ and $R=+20\,\text{cm}$, $\dfrac{1.5}{v}-\dfrac{1}{-100}=\dfrac{0.5}{20}$ gives $\dfrac{1.5}{v}=0.015$ and $v=+100\,\text{cm}$, inside the glass in the direction of propagation.
options.D:
(a) Refraction at a spherical surface follows only the law of reflection, while plane surface refraction follows Snell's law.
(b) The image is always at the pole of the surface.
